label: Error set of two verdict assignments on one common case distribution
term: error set on a common case distribution
definition: Fix one measure μ on a space Ω of cases and two assignments X, Y from cases to verdict values of one type. disagree X Y is the set of cases where X and Y give different values; its μ-measure is the error rate of X against Y on that distribution, and agree X Y is its complement. Every rate compared in one inequality is taken on the same μ; a rate on another distribution (another population, environment or range of cases) is a different quantity.
note: Analyst vocabulary for #1586, attribution deferred. It assumes nothing about independence between error sets. Verdicts may be binary or of any type; binary verdicts are where two errors can cancel (BinaryErrorAccounting). See docs/notes/third-factor-tracking-1586.md.
